subject: Re: Long-context evals — post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Long-context evals — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Alex / Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of your use case
- Ingesting corp-wide documents (policy docs, contracts, meeting transcripts) into a single retrieval context per user.
- Typical session length: 30–100 documents, often multi-GB sets; individual documents range up to ~200k tokens.
- Key concerns: truncation behavior, summarization fidelity across document boundaries, and predictable latency under long-context workloads.

What we recommended on the call
1) Run a focused long-context eval using your representative prompt sets + 3 model families: Redwood-Alpha-large (32k/64k variant), OpenFamily-2-extended, and a quantized Falcon-extended.
2) Benchmarks we'll run: end-to-end token latency, truncation failure modes (where key content is lost), and multi-document summarization fidelity using your evaluation prompts.
3) Validate caching strategy: prefix/KV caching with active-doc caching to avoid re-encoding repeated context.

Immediate next steps (owner)
- Marissa: share initial benchmark harness and prompt sets (today) — see attachments.
- Acme (Alex): confirm 2–3 representative sessions (example exports) we can run in the eval (by Tue).
- Rishi: schedule technical deep-dive with your infra team and provide rough pricing for dedicated burst capacity (by end of week).

Attachments: acme-long-context-benchmarks.csv, acme-prompt-sets-v1.txt, redwood-model-recommendations.pdf

Notes and risks
- If documents exceed model context limits, we'll test two strategies: (a) smart chunking with semantic boundaries + overlap and (b) recency-prioritized truncation. We'll measure summary drift across both.
- We flagged potential quality regressions when switching from 32k to 64k context variants for some models — will surface any regression alerts in the report.

Would you like us to provision a sandbox tenancy for the eval, or do you prefer we run it on Redwood-hosted infra and share results?

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Long-context evals — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks great. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we confirm exports: 

1) Representative sessions: we can pull 3 sessions that are high priority (legal review workflows). The total token count per session averages ~75k tokens, worst-case ~180k. Is it OK if some sessions exceed the largest context size? We're more interested in how truncation strategies affect 'critical-span' retention (e.g., clauses).

2) Sandbox vs Redwood-hosted: we prefer Redwood-hosted for speed, but we need documented controls around data retention and audit logs. Can Rishi/Neha share the SOC2 evidence page and retention policy for sandbox runs?

3) Benchmarks: please include a fidelity score for multi-document summarization (we'll provide the ground-truth summaries). Also include any per-token cost estimates for the different kernel profiles.

We'll aim to provide the exports by Tue EOD. Thanks — Alex

Alex Johnson
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com | +1 617-555-0189

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 12:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Long-context evals — post-call recap and next steps

Alex — perfect, thanks. Responses inline: 

1) Sessions > max context: that's expected for you. We'll run two experimental strategies and report back on the proportion of 'critical-span' tokens preserved. For the long sessions (100k+ tokens) we'll do:
   - Semantic chunking (chunks sized to model window with 20% overlap, boundary-aware by clause)
   - Sliding-window + recency weighting (keep most recent + policy to preserve identified 'contract clauses')
We’ll include an annotation script that marks clause boundaries and the evaluation harness will compute recall of clauses and a summarization ROUGE/F1 + human spot checks.

2) Data controls: Rishi / Neha — can you share the SOC2 evidence page, sandbox retention policy (default 30 days unless overridden), and whether audit logs are accessible to Acme via S3 export? Alex — we can redact PII before ingestion if you prefer.

3) Cost estimates: I've asked Rishi to provide ballpark per-token and per-session pricing for (a) hosted eval runs, (b) dedicated burst capacity, and (c) private deployment. We'll include cost under each model/kernel profile in the final workbook.

Next steps:
- Alex: export 3 sessions and upload to the Drive link I shared (or send a short SFTP note if you need it).
- Rishi/Neha: share SOC2 link + retention/audit answers.

Thanks — will follow up with a calendar invite for the tech deep-dive once Rishi confirms availability.

Best,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Long-context evals — post-call recap and next steps

Hi all —

Quick update from infra/pricing side: 
- SOC2 & compliance: public SOC2 evidence page: https://redwood-internal.example.com/compliance/soc2 (read-only). Sandbox runs inherit the default 30-day retention; we can extend to 90 days on request. Audit logs are exportable to a customer-owned S3 bucket (we'll provide a pre-signed export job).

- Pricing (ballpark):
  * Hosted eval runs: $0.12 / 1k tokens for extended-context variants (includes KV caching).
  * Dedicated burst capacity: quoted as $8,000 / day for a 64k-tailored GPU pool (up to 4k RPS small requests), with a 7-day minimum for initial benchmarking.
  * Private deployment: one-time onboarding + monthly infra fee — we'll provide detailed SOW draft on request.

- Tech deep-dive: I can do Thu 8–10am PT or Fri 1–3pm PT. I’ll schedule for Thu 9am PT and send a calendar invite; please ping if that conflicts.

Attachments included: redwood-model-recommendations.pdf (short notes on kernel choices), acme-long-context-benchmarks.csv (initial harness), acme-prompt-sets-v1.txt (your prompt set from the call).

Rishi
